enum: JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Analytical Cross Sectional Studies
JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Cohort Studies

evidence_quotes.quote: Nuestro análisis estuvo basado en observación participante, conversaciones informales, entrevistas en profundidad, historias de vida, recorridos etnográficos y cartografía social. El proyecto tuvo una duración de dieciocho meses, desde mayo de 2013 hasta octubre de 2014.

evidence_quotes.page: PDF p. 8, Section 'Las geografías desiguales del acceso al agua'
evidence_quotes.quote: En el caso del distrito de riego de María La Baja, cedido en concesión a la Asociación de Usuarios de María La Baja (Usomaría), el cambio en la forma de propiedad y administración del distrito de riego relegó a muchos pobladores locales que no contaban con títulos de propiedad ni con los recursos necesarios para poder hacer parte de la asociación.

evidence_quotes.page: PDF p. 8, Section 'Las geografías desiguales del acceso al agua'
evidence_quotes.quote: Incluso, las parcelas productivas, pequeñas extensiones de tierra adquiridas por pobladores locales bajo figuras comunitarias, no fueron (ni son) tenidas en cuenta por las políticas estatales, ya que sin títulos de propiedad individual no pueden ser incluidas para concesiones de agua.

evidence_quotes.page: PDF p. 9, Section 'Las geografías desiguales del acceso al agua'
evidence_quotes.quote: Éste es también el caso de pobladores que habitan en las inmediaciones de la planta de tratamiento de María La Baja, quienes para poder tener acceso a agua para beber y cocinar deben pedir a los funcionarios de la planta que “les hagan el favor” de llenarles sus tanques y jarras con el líquido tratado (entrevistas personales, María La Baja, julio de 2014).

evidence_quotes.page: PDF p. 9, Section 'Las geografías desiguales del acceso al agua'
evidence_quotes.quote: A pesar de que esta población está ubicada muy cerca de la planta de tratamiento de agua, que hace parte del distrito de riego y desde donde se distribuye el agua tratada al casco urbano de María La Baja, ninguna de las casas cuenta con acueducto ni alcantarillado.

evidence_quotes.criterion: effect_estimate and property enclosure of communal water sources
evidence_quotes.page: PDF p. 9, Section 'Las geografías desiguales del acceso al agua'
evidence_quotes.quote: Jagüeyes (ojos de agua) y reservorios que antes eran de uso comunal y eran la fuente principal del líquido han sido apropiados por grandes propietarios.

country.comment: Case study of the Montes de María region (15 municipalities across the departments of Bolívar and Sucre) in the Colombian Caribbean.
country.where_found: PDF p. 1, Title & Abstract; PDF p. 2, Introduction & Footnote 1

effect_estimate.comment: Purely qualitative ethnographic findings; descriptive secondary land/irrigation area statistics are cited for context (e.g., ~8,500 of 9,688 irrigated hectares in María La Baja devoted to oil palm), with no quantitative causal/associational effect estimate.
effect_estimate.value: Qualitative — no numeric effect estimate reported. State concession/privatization of the María La Baja public irrigation district to the private user association Usomaría excluded local peasants without individual property titles or financial resources to join, as well as communal parcels ('parcelas productivas') ineligible for water concessions without individual deeds, concentrating ~8,500 of 9,688 irrigated hectares in oil palm monocultures and excluding small livestock/dairy producers. Surrounding rural settlements lack formal piped water and sewerage connections (even adjacent to the María La Baja treatment plant, which serves only the urban core), forcing households to rely on latrines, discretionary favors from plant staff, or agrochemical-contaminated and seasonally dry irrigation canals; across Montes de María, monoculture expansion backed by coerced/formalized titling (Law 1182 of 2008), productive alliances, and private security also enclosed, dried up, or contaminated formerly communal springs ('jagüeyes') and reservoirs and restricted open defecation access.
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF pp. 6–11, Sections 'Las promesas rotas del desarrollo', 'Las geografías desiguales del acceso al agua', and 'Espacios del miedo y regímenes de inmovilidad'

mechanism_certainty.comment: Design ceiling for a primary qualitative study (CASP) is 2. Through 18 months of ethnographic fieldwork, interviews with residents and the Usomaría manager, and social cartography, the study directly observes and documents how individual-title eligibility rules for water concessions, association membership/water fees, exclusionary service areas around the treatment plant and irrigation canals, private discretionary control over dam gates and plant water handouts, and private property enclosure of communal springs restrict water and sanitation access.
mechanism_certainty.where_found: PDF p. 3, Footnote 5; PDF pp. 8–11, Sections 'Las geografías desiguales del acceso al agua' and 'Espacios del miedo y regímenes de inmovilidad'

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines individual property title requirements and exclusion of untitled/informal ('falsa tradición') and communal tenure ('parcelas productivas') from water concessions and Usomaría membership, formalization/titling pressures under Law 1182 of 2008, private enclosure of communal water sources, service-area exclusion of rural settlements next to the irrigation district and urban-serving treatment plant (and exclusion of non-palm pasture use), membership/water payment barriers, and discretionary gate releases and informal 'favors' by treatment plant staff.
mechanism_flags.value: ELIGIBILITY, BURDEN, DISCRETION_ACCOMMODATION, tenure, property, documentation, service_area, fees, discretion
mechanism_flags.where_found: PDF pp. 6–7, Section 'Las promesas rotas del desarrollo'; PDF pp. 8–9, Section 'Las geografías desiguales del acceso al agua'

outcome_flags.comment: Documents restricted domestic and productive water access, exclusion from formal water concessions and absence of piped aqueduct/sewerage connections in La Suprema, contamination of water sources by palm agrochemicals and livestock waste causing diarrheal and skin illness, seasonal drying and palm-dictated release schedules in irrigation canals, and reliance on latrines plus threats against open defecation in palm plantations.
outcome_flags.where_found: PDF pp. 8–9, Section 'Las geografías desiguales del acceso al agua'; PDF p. 11, Section 'Espacios del miedo y regímenes de inmovilidad'

publication_year.comment: Accepted 23 February 2015, modified 1 June 2015, published in Revista de Estudios Sociales No. 54 (October–December 2015), DOI 10.7440/res54.2015.08.
publication_year.where_found: PDF p. 1, article header; PDF p. 2, running header

risk_of_bias_tool.comment: Primary qualitative collaborative ethnographic study using participant observation, interviews, life histories, ethnographic walks, and social cartography; appraised with CASP Qualitative Checklist per RISK_OF_BIAS.md §1.
risk_of_bias_tool.where_found: PDF p. 1, Abstract; PDF p. 3, Introduction & Footnote 5

sample_size.comment: Total number of participants, interviews, or communities is not reported in the text. The paper reports 1 regional case study (Montes de María, spanning 15 municipalities) with fieldwork conducted across 6 visits of 1 to 4 weeks each over 18 months (May 2013–October 2014), and lists 16 specific cited interviews in the References section ('Entrevistas', items 62–77).
sample_size.where_found: PDF p. 3, Introduction & Footnote 5; PDF p. 13, 'Entrevistas' (items 62–77)

study_design.comment: Authors explicitly describe a collaborative ethnographic study ('métodos etnográficos llevados a cabo bajo los lineamientos de la investigación colaborativa') conducted over 18 months (May 2013–October 2014) across 6 field visits.
study_design.value: Collaborative ethnographic case study (participant observation, informal conversations, in-depth interviews, life histories, ethnographic walks, and social cartography)
study_design.where_found: PDF p. 1, Abstract; PDF p. 3, Introduction & Footnote 5
